who: Historian of South Asia at Vanderbilt University; DPhil, Oxford (Wolfson College).

evidence.says: LC identifies Sheikh's Oxford modern-history DPhil thesis, State and society in Gujarat, with Wolfson College, and identifies her as a Vanderbilt history professor.
Vanderbilt identifies Samira Sheikh as a historian of South Asia and associate professor of history, with an Oxford DPhil listed as 2004.
Vanderbilt's repository names Samira Sheikh as committee chair of Ashish Koul's 2017 history PhD, Making New Muslim Arains.

notes: The LC record matches both the supervisor's doctoral college and university affiliation; the listed student's repository record confirms supervision.

who: Historian of ancient Greece at the University of Michigan; PhD Princeton, 1997.

evidence.says: LC identifies Sara Forsdyke as a professor of classical studies and history at Michigan and cites her 1997 work on exile and Athenian political development.
Michigan's faculty profile lists a Princeton PhD in 1997 and research in the social, political and legal history of Archaic and Classical Greece.
The December 2013 appointment record states that Forsdyke joined Michigan in 1997, became professor in 2012, and was appointed classical studies chair for 2014-2017 while also professor of history.

notes: The authority identity, Princeton doctorate and Michigan career agree with the supervisor record and students' period and field.

who: Historian of ancient warfare at Florida International University; PhD archaeology, University College London, 2001.

evidence.says: LC links Gwyn Davies to Roman siege works (2006), whose author teaches at Florida International University, and to TRAC 2000 (2001).
Davies's institutional CV lists a 2001 archaeology PhD from UCL, FIU history appointments beginning in 2001, associate professor from 2008, and the same Roman Siege Works and TRAC publications.
FIU identifies Gwyn Davies as an associate professor specializing in ancient and military history, including graduate teaching on the First and Second World Wars.

notes: Select nb2001071862: its FIU affiliation and distinctive publications match the institutional CV, which also confirms the AHA doctoral institution.

who: Beverly Jo Bossler, historian of imperial China at UC Davis; PhD UC Berkeley, 1991 according to her CV.

evidence.says: LC connects Beverly Jo Bossler to her 1991 doctorate, Powerful relations and relations of power, and identifies her as the UC Davis historian of imperial China employed there from 1992.
Her CV gives a UC Berkeley PhD in 1991 and UC Davis appointments from 1992, with promotion to professor in 2005; it lists Powerful Relations and other works on imperial China.
UC Davis identifies Bossler as professor emerita, with a history doctorate from Berkeley and research on Tang, Song and Yuan China.

notes: AHA gives 1992 for the doctorate; the institutional CV and LC thesis citation give 1991. Affiliation, field, full name and works establish the match despite this one-year discrepancy.

who: Joan Cameron Bristol, historian of colonial Latin America at George Mason University; PhD Pennsylvania, 2001.

evidence.says: LC identifies Joan Cameron Bristol as a professor in George Mason's Department of History and Art History and author of Christians, blasphemers, and witches.
The faculty profile names the same book and Pennsylvania doctorate, and explicitly lists David McKenzie's 2021 and John Rodriguez's 2018 dissertations under Dissertations Supervised.
George Mason's faculty catalogue lists Joan C. Bristol, associate professor of history, with a University of Pennsylvania PhD in 2001.

notes: Both listed students and their dissertation titles and years match her faculty profile exactly.

who: Scot Brown, historian of African American history and popular culture at UCLA; Cornell history doctorate, 1999.

evidence.says: LC identifies Scot Brown as author of Fighting for US and cites UCLA faculty pages identifying him as a history and African American studies professor.
UCLA's faculty page lists Fighting for Us and his Cornell dissertation, The US Organization: African-American Cultural Nationalism in the Era of Black Power, dated August 1999.
UCLA's 2012-2013 PhD list names Scot Brown as chair for both Melanie Arias and Robert Earl Baker, including Baker's Push Back dissertation.

notes: The candidate's works and institution agree, and UCLA directly confirms supervision of both listed students. UCLA gives Arias's final dissertation title as Experimental Citizens.

who: Andy Bruno, historian of Soviet environmental history, formerly Northern Illinois University; PhD Illinois Urbana-Champaign, 2011.

evidence.says: LC identifies Andy Bruno as author of The Nature of Soviet Power (2016), then assistant professor of history and faculty associate in environmental studies at Northern Illinois University.

His CV lists a 2011 Illinois Urbana-Champaign history PhD, NIU employment in 2012-2024, and The Nature of Soviet Power. It names Alexander Sosenko as his NIU PhD advisee in 2024 and Alexander Craver as a current NIU PhD advisee.
Wisconsin's academic profile identifies Bruno with NIU history and environmental studies and research on Soviet environmental history, including The Nature of Soviet Power.

notes: Degree, authority-linked book and both listed advisees match. The CV records his move to Indiana University in 2024 while still listing Craver as a current NIU advisee.

who: Evan Burr Bukey, historian of modern Germany and Austria at the University of Arkansas; PhD Ohio State, 1969.

evidence.says: LC identifies Evan Burr Bukey as author of Hitler's hometown (1986).

Ohio Wesleyan's citation identifies Evan B. Bukey, his Ohio State doctorate in 1969, his Arkansas faculty appointment beginning in 1969, and his book Hitler's Hometown: Linz, Austria, 1908-1945 (1986).
Arkansas identifies Bukey as a specialist in modern German and Austrian history who joined its history department in 1969 and retired in 2008; it names Hitler's Hometown among his books.

notes: The authority's distinctive book matches the university sources; doctoral institution and year agree, and Arkansas employment covers both students' dissertation years.
